Sunshine is a European import set in Hungary between 1880 and 1980, it's the epic story of Hungarian Jews, the Sonnenschein family. This name literally translates to Sunshine. The family has humble beginnings, then is prosperous, becomes upwardly mobile, changes it's name, and hopes to assimilate into Hungarian society so successive generations can advance professionally. The story is told through the eyes of the eldest son in each of three generations; Ralph Fiennes plays these three roles. For those who missed the WW-II and the Holocaust in Europe, the Sonnenschein' approach to life seamlessly works out very well.

Sunshine is being acclaimed as an artistic success. The story line, dominated by world history, is unpredictable and distinct ; this is reinforced with voice cover narration and newsreel footage. The family 'plot' lurches from one unpredictable event [ie. the Hapsburgs, WW-I, WW-II, Fascism, Communism, etc.] to the next with continuity, depth and much detail. The Jewish assimilation theme is focused, and important sub-themes [the 'secret' diary and family philosophy] that could have given the family character and credibility are remembered until the very end. Alternatively, the filmmakers provide generation continuity using common themes of incest / infidelity.

Ralph Fiennes exhibits flashes of brilliance, his performance is award winning material. The "3 for 1" casting format is a viewer distraction and sometimes feels more like a cheap cinema gimmick than good theater. Sunshine is basically Hungarian "History Channel" material. Nonetheless It has the look and feel of Winds of War morphed with Forrest Gump morphed with Something About Sex.

Good action sequences, plenty of "feel good" scenes, a good musical score, and the part that really makes the movie stand out is the compelling performances. Especially by Robert De Niro. The story of Men of Honor is focused on Carl Brashear, played by Cuba Gooding Jr., who wants to be the first African American deep sea diver in the navy. It chronicles his inspiring journey from being a poor farmer to getting into diving school and even further. It is a powerful story, and while the theme of perseverance against all odds has been explored before, this film brings a fresh and heartfelt perspective to it. A person, against all of the odds, won't give up until they accomplish their goals that they set for some sentimental reason many years ago. It feels authentic, and the struggles Brashear faces in the movie, including the C.O. of the diving school tampering with his final test, add tension and drama to the narrative. All of this is elevated by the scene when Robert De Niro finally enters the movie. De Niro plays Master Chief Sunday, the teacher at the diving school Brashear is attending.
